<p class="person-bio">
I’m interested in the abiotic and biotic drivers of ecological stability. Specifically, I develop concepts and methods for assessing the role of response diversity in driving stability, and I use ecoacoustic data to quantify ecosystem dynamics, change, and stability in real-world ecosystems. In my spare time, I enjoy reading, going to the cinema, drinking matcha lattes, and being Kyoto's least-requested DJ.
</p>

<p class="person-keywords-jp">
生態系の安定性・応答の多様性・音響モニタリング
</p>

<div class="jp-person-name">Ecoacoustics · Species interactions · Response diversity</div>

<p class="person-position">
<strong>Fully funded PhD</strong> | Linköping University, Sweden
</p>

<div class="vacancy-meta">

<strong>Project:</strong> Species interaction networks and response diversity in soundscapes  
<strong>Host institution:</strong> Linköping University, Sweden  
<strong>Main supervisor:</strong> Prof. Anna Eklöf  
<strong>Co-supervisor:</strong> Dr Samuel R.P-J. Ross (Kyoto University), Dr Sara Keen (Earth Species Project)  
<strong>Application deadline:</strong> 5 October 2026

</div>

<p class="person-bio">
We are recruiting a fully funded PhD student to apply ecoacoustics to the study of species interactions and response diversity. 
</p>

<p class="person-bio">
The position is part of the wider ReDiLEEP Doctoral Network, which brings together researchers across Europe and beyond to investigate how response diversity contributes to ecological resilience and stability.
</p>

<p class="person-bio">
<strong>Eligibility:</strong> EU mobility rules apply. Applicants are not eligible if they have resided or carried out their main activity in Sweden for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before recruitment.
</p>

<p class="person-keywords-jp">
Ecoacoustics · Species interactions · Response diversity
</p>
